clue.text: Splendour of chapter in uplifting story

indicators.note: in places the chapter's letter inside the upturned story
in a down clue, uplifting means the word for story is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a story is a tale

explanation.surface: A reader praising the splendour of one chapter in an inspiring tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns TALE upwards to ELAT, and 'in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliance or showy success, a dazzling display, close to splendour.

clue.text: Italian staple Romeo's consumed, starters of marinated Ischian beef

indicators.note: consumed means the pasta eats up the Romeo letter, holding it inside

parts.note: pasta is the staple food of Italy
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: starters of means the opening letters of the next two words are used

explanation.surface: A menu note: pasta for Romeo, with a beef dish marinated in Ischia to start.
explanation.walkthrough: PASTA swallows R to make PASTRA; M and I come from the starts of 'marinated Ischian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned, smoked and cured beef, often served sliced in sandwiches.

clue.text: Busier railway traversing mountains

indicators.note: traversing means the answer runs across the two words, lying inside them

explanation.surface: A busier rail line crossing a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Busier' into the start of 'railway'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged range of peaks, as in the Sierra Nevada.

clue.text: Working dad from university city a key literary figure

indicators.note: working means the letters of dad from are worked into a new order

parts.note: Oxford is a famous English university city

explanation.surface: A working father from Oxford hailed as an important writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges DAD FROM into FORD MAD, and OXFORD follows. Ford and Mini, Maxi and others are car names, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford Madox Ford was an important English novelist and editor, author of The Good Soldier.

clue.text: Country dance one of the Bee Gees picked up

indicators.note: picked up means the name is caught by ear, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: Maurice Gibb was one of the three brothers in the Bee Gees

explanation.surface: A Bee Gee doing a rustic dance.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent Maurice sounds like the other word; the Bee Gees were a pop group of three brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Morris dancing is a traditional English folk dance with bells and sticks, often seen at village fetes.

clue.text: Recover bullet following shot to leg

indicators.note: following places the bullet after the shot

parts.note: in cricket, a pull is a stroke hitting the ball to the leg side
a round is a single bullet or cartridge

explanation.surface: A wounded man trying to recover after being shot in the leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg is the cricket field's leg side, not a body part; a pull is a cross-batted shot there.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull round is an idiom meaning to get better after an illness.

clue.text: Prison car turned into material for recycling

indicators.note: turned into means the letters of prison car become something else in a new order

explanation.surface: An old prison van being converted into recyclable metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap iron is discarded metal collected to be melted down and reused.

clue.text: Concentrate of spun copper sulphate, primarily

indicators.note: spun means the little word of is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of sulphate is taken

explanation.surface: A chemistry note on a concentrated solution of copper sulphate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concentrate' looks like a noun in chemistry, but it is the verb; 'spun' turns OF into FO.
explanation.definitionFit: To focus is to direct all attention onto one thing, which is to concentrate.

clue.text: City of Nassau's tiny

indicators.note: of signals a part taken from what follows, here letters lying in the words

explanation.surface: A remark that the Bahamas' capital is small.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the end of Nassau's and the start of 'tiny'.
explanation.definitionFit: Austin is the state capital of Texas.

clue.text: Criminally trap golden eagle?

indicators.note: criminally means the letters of trap are bent, reworked into another order

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Illegally trapping a golden eagle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golden' looks like a description of the eagle, but it supplies the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A raptor is any bird of prey, of which an eagle is one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Odd, receiving odd tattoo?

indicators.note: receiving means the first word takes the second into its middle

parts.note: droll means amusingly odd
rum is old British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone eccentric getting an eccentric tattoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tattoo' looks like body art, but it means a rhythmic drumbeat, as in a military tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo can be a rapid rhythmic beating of drums, as a drumroll is.

clue.text: Mum sadly rejected peaceful greeting

indicators.note: rejected means the whole lot is sent back, read in the other direction

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum
alas is a sad exclamation

explanation.surface: A mother sadly turned away despite offering a friendly greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: MA ALAS reads backwards as SALAAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Salaam is an Arabic greeting meaning peace, often given with a low bow.

clue.text: See 4
Maybe Top Gear host works with VW

indicators.note: works means the letters are worked up into a new order

explanation.surface: A television presenter putting a Volkswagen through its paces.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Gear is a BBC motoring programme; HOST and VW are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Gear is an example of a television programme, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Academic stream swindles auto parts

parts.note: the Cam is the river through the university city of Cambridge
to shaft is slang for to cheat or swindle

explanation.surface: A university course swindling people out of car parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Academic stream' looks like a course of study; it is a river flowing past colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: A camshaft is a rotating shaft in an engine that works the valves.

clue.text: I must move to the back of fancy cinema, very large

indicators.text: must move to the back of
indicators.note: must move to the back of means the letter I leaves the front and goes to the end

parts.note: IMAX is a big-screen cinema format

explanation.surface: An instruction to sit at the back of a big swanky cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: IMAX with its I sent to the back gives MAXI.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxi is an adjective for extra long or extra big, as in a maxi skirt.

clue.text: Ms Dorries is on the way back after leaving Ulster's American-style saloon

indicators.note: after leaving means the Ulster letters depart
on the way back means the remaining letters are read from right to left

parts.note: Nadine Dorries is a former British politician; with the 's for is it gives her name plus S
NI, Northern Ireland, is Ulster; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A politician returning home from Northern Ireland in an American car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' turns NADINES into SENIDAN before 'after leaving' takes NI out. A saloon is the British word for a four-door car.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedan is the American term for the car body style called a saloon in Britain.

clue.text: Pasteur occasionally embraced by nurse (heavenly body!)

indicators.note: embraced by means the letters from Pasteur are held inside the nurse

parts.note: SRN, State Registered Nurse, was a British nursing qualification

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of Pasteur is used

explanation.surface: The scientist Pasteur hugged by a nurse, with an exclamation at its celestial feel.
explanation.walkthrough: SRN is an old British nursing qualification, a crossword staple; 'occasionally' takes Pasteur's even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is the ringed planet, sixth from the Sun.

clue.text: Skirt the road to Leeds, followed by van from Ilkley

parts.note: road signs show the way to Leeds as the M1 North, written MI N

indicators.note: van means front, so the front letter of Ilkley is taken

explanation.surface: Driving the motorway to Leeds behind a van from Ilkley, a Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' looks like a verb, to go round the road, but it is the garment. The M1 is the motorway from London north to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A mini is a very short skirt, popular from the 1960s.

clue.text: More than one eminent musician from West perhaps arranges to come over

parts.note: Mae West, the Hollywood actress, is one person called West

indicators.note: to come over means the word for arranges is flipped, read from the end

parts.note: to sort is to arrange

explanation.surface: Several noted musicians from the West organising a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like a direction; it is the actress Mae West. SORTS reads backwards as STROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestros are distinguished conductors or composers, masters of music.

clue.text: Accompany notorious conquistador when cycling

indicators.note: cycling means letters are moved round from one end to the other

parts.note: Hernan Cortes was the Spanish conqueror of the Aztecs

explanation.surface: Going along with an infamous Spanish conqueror on a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: Move CORT from the front of CORTES to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort is to go along with someone as a guide or guard.

clue.text: Muse knocked over an item in the garage

indicators.note: in a down clue, knocked over means the Muse's name is upended

parts.note: Clio is the Greek Muse of history

explanation.surface: Someone musing after knocking something over in the garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a verb, but it is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilcan holds lubricating oil and is a familiar object in a workshop or car garage.

clue.text: Persian ruler giving Roman 6 king a going-over

indicators.note: a going-over means both words are flipped over, read backwards

parts.note: sex is the Latin word for six
rex is Latin for king

explanation.surface: A ruler giving a sixth-placed Roman king a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman 6' looks like VI, but it is the Latin word for six.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerxes the Great was a king of the Achaemenid Persian Empire.

clue.text: See if you can beat setter's flower arrangement

parts.note: a challenge to beat someone is to race them
the setter refers to himself as me; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A setter challenging solvers to outdo a floral arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RACE ME, the setter's challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A raceme is a flower cluster in which flowers grow on short stalks along a central stem.

clue.text: Junior team in organdie skirts

indicators.note: skirts means the words go round the answer, which lies inside them

explanation.surface: A youth team wearing organdie skirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' looks like clothing, but it is a verb: the words surround the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor means a younger person, one below legal adult age.

clue.text: This man's composed, noted Boris, when introduced by the Queen?

indicators.note: the Queen's cut-glass accent says off as orff, so the name is what is heard

parts.note: Boris Karloff was the famous horror film actor

explanation.surface: A famous Boris being presented by the Queen as a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: In the upper-class British accent associated with the royals, 'off' is said 'orff'.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Orff was the German composer of Carmina Burana; this man's composed means this is a composer.

clue.text: See 4
About a pint knocked back, Tom loves it!

parts.note: c, circa, means about

indicators.note: knocked back means the pint is turned back to front, read backwards

explanation.surface: A man called Tom downing about a pint and loving it.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom is a male cat, not a drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Catnip is a plant whose scent excites cats, so a tomcat delights in it.

clue.text: Street hip-hop beat

parts.note: rap is a genre of hip-hop music

explanation.surface: A street hip-hop rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like a musical rhythm, but it is the verb to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: To strap someone is to thrash them with a leather belt, an old punishment.

clue.text: Father, ordinary male, declared bankruptcy in South Korea after this

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
the won is South Korea's currency, so a bankrupt there might say no won

explanation.surface: A priest and an ordinary man going broke in South Korea.
explanation.definitionFit: From now on is an idiom meaning henceforth, starting at this moment.
